rules.summary: Require active component attributes to match one explicitly declared allowed tuple.

authorities.title: OASIS TOSCA Version 2.0 - Requirements and Capabilities

problem_shapes: Two selected components are compatible only for an explicit finite set of attribute-value pairs.
encode_steps: Bind the left and right component IDs in subject order.
Resolve one explicit allowed-pair declaration and both finite attribute domains.
Guard the allowed-tuple disjunction by conjunction of the two component selection bits.
anti_patterns: Do not infer compatibility from equal labels unless that tuple is explicitly allowed.
Do not create enum labels or wildcard tuples outside the declared finite domains.
escalate_when: Escalate arithmetic, regex, or open-world attribute matching to a richer primitive.

solver_encoding.verification: assert the guarded allowed-tuple disjunction over complete attributes
solver_encoding.synthesis: leave only explicitly declared finite attribute or selection fields free
formula: not (selected(left) and selected(right)) or any((left_attribute = u) and (right_attribute = v) for (u, v) in allowed)

rules.summary: Forbid two declared components from being selected together.

authorities.title: Debian Policy Manual - Conflicting Binary Packages

problem_shapes: Two packages, features, or implementations are mutually incompatible.
encode_steps: Bind exactly two distinct declared component IDs.
Resolve both selection bits before lowering the pair exclusion.
Assert that at least one of the two selections is false.
anti_patterns: Do not infer conflicts from version names or external package metadata.
Do not encode a directional replacement relation as symmetric exclusion.
escalate_when: Escalate conditional or many-way conflicts to explicit guarded rules.

solver_encoding.verification: assert pairwise exclusion over complete component selections
solver_encoding.synthesis: leave only explicitly declared component selection bits free

rules.summary: Require a selected consumer to select at least one declared provider.

problem_shapes: A selected feature, package, or component needs one provider from an explicit finite alternative set.
encode_steps: Put the consumer first and every admissible provider after it in subjects.
Resolve every subject against declared component facts before allocating variables.
Guard the provider disjunction with the consumer selection bit.
anti_patterns: Do not infer providers from names, package repositories, or undeclared capabilities.
Do not use this rule for a requirement that needs every provider.
escalate_when: Escalate ordered, weighted, or cardinality-constrained provider choices to separate primitives.

solver_encoding.verification: assert the guarded disjunction over complete component selections
solver_encoding.synthesis: leave only explicitly declared component selection bits free
formula: not selected(consumer) or selected(provider_1) or ... or selected(provider_n)

rules.summary: Enforce declared inclusive selection bounds for an active finite component group.

problem_shapes: An optional or active finite group permits a bounded number of selected members.
encode_steps: Bind one declared selection-group ID as the subject.
Validate non-empty unique membership and 0 <= minimum <= maximum <= member count.
Force every member off when the group is inactive and apply both inclusive bounds when active.
anti_patterns: Do not count components that are not declared members of the group.
Do not silently repair inverted or out-of-range bounds.
escalate_when: Escalate nested or weighted choices to separate explicit constraints.

solver_encoding.verification: assert the guarded lower and upper bounds over complete member selections
solver_encoding.synthesis: leave only explicitly declared group or member selection fields free

rules.summary: Require a selected provider version rank to lie within a consumer's declared inclusive interval.

problem_shapes: A selected consumer requires a selected provider from one caller-ranked inclusive version interval.
encode_steps: Bind the consumer first and provider second.
Resolve the consumer requirement and require the same declared ordering on the provider rank.
Guard provider selection and both inclusive rank comparisons with consumer selection.
anti_patterns: Do not parse SemVer or infer precedence from version strings.
Do not compare ranks from different or undeclared ordering IDs.
escalate_when: Escalate disjoint ranges, prerelease policy, or semantic version parsing to separate preprocessing or primitives.

solver_encoding.verification: assert provider selection and inclusive rank bounds over complete ranked-version facts
solver_encoding.synthesis: leave only explicitly declared provider selection or bounded rank fields free
formula: not selected(consumer) or (selected(provider) and minimum_rank <= rank(provider) and rank(provider) <= maximum_rank)

rules.summary: Require every declared integer term cell to be present and resolvable and every checked linear term to contribute to one exact integer target.

problem_shapes: A finite explicitly listed set of integer facts must satisfy one exact weighted balance.
encode_steps: Bind exactly one aggregate-balance definition ID as the subject.
Resolve every explicitly listed term to a present integer cell and validate each checked integer coefficient.
Include every explicitly listed term in the exact weighted sum and equate it to the target.
anti_patterns: Do not infer decimal tolerance, rounding, units, or undeclared contributing rows.
Do not condition term presence or arithmetic contribution on row activity.
Do not accept coefficient overflow or nonlinear multiplication.
escalate_when: Escalate decimal arithmetic, tolerance bands, currency conversion, dynamic term discovery, or nonlinear formulas outside this primitive.

solver_encoding.verification: fix every listed integer cell and assert unconditional presence plus exact weighted equality
solver_encoding.synthesis: constrain only explicitly unknown listed cell presence or integer values within their field domains
formula: for every listed term t: present(t)
sum over every listed term t of coefficient(t) * value(t) = target

valid.expectation: exact integer balance 100 plus negative 30 equals 70

invalid.expectation: counterexample because 100 plus negative 30 does not equal 69

rules.summary: Keep the number of active rows in a relation or declared row subset within inclusive integer bounds.

problem_shapes: A finite relation or explicitly declared row subset must contain between minimum and maximum active rows.
encode_steps: Bind exactly one cardinality definition ID as the subject.
Resolve the whole relation or its declared row subset in caller order.
Sum each row activity Boolean as a zero-one integer and constrain the inclusive lower and upper bounds.
anti_patterns: Do not count inactive rows or infer rows outside the declared finite relation.
Do not use exclusive bounds or silently swap inverted bounds.
escalate_when: Escalate unbounded populations, grouped counts, or aggregate predicates beyond active-row membership outside this primitive.

solver_encoding.verification: fix row activity and assert the inclusive active-row count interval
solver_encoding.synthesis: constrain explicitly unknown row activity bits while preserving the declared finite row set
formula: minimum <= sum over declared rows of ite(active(row), 1, 0) <= maximum

valid.expectation: one active row satisfies the inclusive range 1 through 4

invalid.expectation: counterexample because zero active rows is below the inclusive minimum 1

rules.summary: Require one field to be present when an active row has a present trigger field equal to a schema-typed expected value.

problem_shapes: A typed trigger value on an active row conditionally requires another field to be present.
encode_steps: Bind exactly one conditional-requirement definition ID as the subject.
Resolve the trigger and required fields and validate the expected value against the trigger field domain.
Guard required-field presence by row activity, trigger presence, and typed equality with the expected value.
anti_patterns: Do not fire the condition when the trigger field is absent.
Do not coerce strings, integers, enums, or Booleans across field domains.
Do not infer a required value; this rule owns only presence.
escalate_when: Escalate compound predicates, regex conditions, cross-row triggers, or value synthesis beyond conditional presence outside this primitive.

solver_encoding.verification: fix the complete row and assert required-field presence whenever the typed trigger is present and equal to expected
solver_encoding.synthesis: constrain explicitly unknown trigger values or required-field presence while preserving declared field domains
formula: active(row) and present(row,trigger) and value(row,trigger) = expected implies present(row,required)

valid.expectation: the active pro row supplies its required region

invalid.expectation: counterexample because the active pro row omits its required region

rules.summary: Require every active child row with a complete key to match one active parent row with a complete corresponding key, using MATCH SIMPLE semantics.

authorities.title: PostgreSQL CREATE TABLE - Referential Actions and MATCH Types

problem_shapes: Every complete finite child key must have one equal complete parent key.
encode_steps: Bind exactly one foreign-key definition ID as the subject.
Resolve equal-arity, type-compatible child and parent fields before lowering.
For each active child with a complete key, finitely disjoin all active complete parent-row matches.
anti_patterns: Do not require a match for an incomplete child key; this profile uses MATCH SIMPLE.
Do not infer parents outside the declared finite relation or coerce key types.
Do not encode the join with quantifiers or arrays.
escalate_when: Escalate MATCH FULL, cascading mutations, deferred transactions, or unbounded parent relations outside this profile.

solver_encoding.verification: fix child and parent rows and assert a finite parent-match disjunction for each complete active child key
solver_encoding.synthesis: constrain only explicitly unknown row activity, key presence, or typed key values
formula: active(child) and complete_C(child) implies some parent row is active, complete_P(parent), and equal on every corresponding key field

valid.expectation: complete child key matches and absent child key is ignored under MATCH SIMPLE

invalid.expectation: counterexample because complete child key 8 has no parent match

rules.summary: Require all participating fields on each active row to be present and equal one explicitly allowed schema-typed tuple.

authorities.title: SHACL 1.2 Core - Value and Logical Constraint Components

problem_shapes: A finite tuple of typed fields on every active row must belong to one explicit allowed relation.
encode_steps: Bind exactly one consistency-relation definition ID as the subject.
Resolve the ordered fields and validate every allowed tuple for arity and schema-typed values.
For each active row require all tuple fields to be present and finitely disjoin equality with each allowed tuple.
anti_patterns: Do not infer wildcard tuples, create enum labels, or accept partial active-row tuples.
Do not coerce values across field domains or encode the finite relation with quantifiers.
escalate_when: Escalate open-world tuple sets, regex matching, computed tuple members, or relations too large for finite expansion outside this primitive.

solver_encoding.verification: fix complete rows and assert active-row membership in the finite allowed tuple relation
solver_encoding.synthesis: constrain explicitly unknown participating field presence or typed values to one allowed tuple
formula: active(row) implies complete_F(row) and some allowed tuple equals value(row,F) componentwise

valid.expectation: the tuple pro and eu belongs to the finite allowed relation

invalid.expectation: counterexample because the tuple free and eu is not allowed

rules.summary: Require active rows to have present integer endpoints with start before end and every declared predecessor to finish no later than its active successor starts.

problem_shapes: Active finite interval rows must be nonempty and declared predecessor edges must respect finish-start order.
encode_steps: Bind exactly one temporal-constraint definition ID as the subject.
Resolve integer start and end fields plus every before and after row ID.
Require present endpoints and strict start-before-end for each active row.
For each edge require an active successor to have an active predecessor whose end is no later than the successor start.
anti_patterns: Do not permit zero-length or reversed active intervals.
Do not infer predecessor edges, durations, time zones, or overlap relations beyond the declared finish-start ordering.
Do not interpret finite integer order as wall-clock transaction semantics.
escalate_when: Escalate Allen relations beyond before or meets, calendar arithmetic, time zones, recurrence, or unbounded interval sets outside this primitive.

solver_encoding.verification: fix all finite rows and assert strict interval validity plus each declared predecessor implication
solver_encoding.synthesis: constrain explicitly unknown activity, endpoint presence, or integer endpoint values within the finite schema bounds
formula: active(row) implies present(start) and present(end) and start < end
for every before -> after edge: active(after) implies active(before) and end(before) <= start(after)

valid.expectation: both intervals are strict and predecessor end 4 is no later than successor start 4

invalid.expectation: counterexample from reversed successor interval and predecessor end 6 after successor start 5

rules.summary: Require active rows with complete keys to differ on at least one key field, using SQL-like NULLS DISTINCT semantics.

problem_shapes: Active rows with complete scalar or composite keys must not duplicate another complete key.
encode_steps: Bind exactly one unique-constraint definition ID as the subject.
Resolve its relation and ordered key fields against the strict finite snapshot.
For each ordered active row pair with both keys complete, require at least one corresponding key value to differ.
anti_patterns: Do not treat absent key cells as equal; this profile uses NULLS DISTINCT.
Do not add a synthetic sentinel for absence or coerce mismatched field domains.
Do not infer uniqueness beyond the finite declared rows.
escalate_when: Escalate NULLS NOT DISTINCT, collation-sensitive strings, expression indexes, or unbounded relations outside this profile.

solver_encoding.verification: fix the complete bounded snapshot and assert pairwise distinctness only for active rows with complete keys
solver_encoding.synthesis: constrain only explicitly unknown row activity, key presence, or typed key values
formula: for every ordered row pair r < s: active(r) and active(s) and complete_K(r) and complete_K(s) implies some f in K has value(r,f) != value(s,f)

valid.expectation: distinct complete keys pass and the absent key is ignored under NULLS DISTINCT

invalid.expectation: counterexample from equal complete active keys

rules.summary: Require every present value of one integer field on an active row to lie within inclusive declared bounds.

authorities.title: SHACL 1.2 Core - Value Range Constraint Components

problem_shapes: Present integer cells on active rows must lie inside one inclusive interval.
encode_steps: Bind exactly one value-range definition ID as the subject.

rules.summary: Assign one declared job to exactly one machine and integer start tick inside the finite horizon.

authorities.title: Multiproject Scheduling with Limited Resources: A Zero-One Programming Approach

problem_shapes: Every required finite job must receive one machine and one non-preemptive start tick.
encode_steps: Bind exactly one declared job ID as the subject.
Enumerate only machine/start pairs whose positive duration completes within the integer horizon.
Require the sum of the job's bounded zero-one placement variables to equal one.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a feasible assignment as proof of optimality.
Do not infer machines, durations, or continuous-time placements outside caller facts.
escalate_when: Escalate preemption, continuous time, or optional jobs to a different scheduling model.

solver_encoding.verification: fix the observed assignment and assert exactly one active bounded placement
solver_encoding.synthesis: leave only explicitly declared assignment unknowns free over the finite placement domain

invalid.expectation: no exactly-once placement exists within the declared horizon

rules.summary: Keep every declared resource's concurrent non-preemptive demand within one machine's capacity at every horizon tick.

authorities.title: Multiproject Scheduling with Limited Resources: A Zero-One Programming Approach

problem_shapes: Concurrent jobs on one machine consume finite integer resource capacities over discrete ticks.
encode_steps: Bind exactly one declared machine ID as the subject.
For every declared resource and horizon tick, select placements active at that tick.
Require the sum of each active job demand times its zero-one placement to fit machine capacity.
anti_patterns: Do not check only job start ticks; demand applies throughout each half-open execution interval.
Do not infer undeclared resources, fractional ticks, or dynamic capacity.
escalate_when: Escalate preemption, variable demand profiles, or calendar-dependent capacity to a richer scheduling model.

solver_encoding.verification: assert every per-resource per-tick capacity inequality over observed assignments
solver_encoding.synthesis: enforce every capacity inequality over explicitly declared bounded assignment unknowns
formula: for every machine m, resource r, and tick tau: sum demand(j,r) * placement(j,m,t) where t <= tau < t + duration(j,m) <= capacity(m,r)

rules.summary: Minimize the latest job completion during synthesis or enforce an explicit maximum makespan during verification.

authorities.title: Multiproject Scheduling with Limited Resources: A Zero-One Programming Approach

problem_shapes: Optimize the latest completion of a finite set of non-preemptive jobs after hard feasibility rules are declared.
Verify a complete observed schedule against one explicit hard maximum makespan.
encode_steps: Bind every makespan-scoped job ID as a subject and derive each completion from its unique placement.
Introduce one bounded integer makespan at least every subject completion.
In synthesis emit the typed minimize objective; in verification require maximum_makespan and emit only its hard upper bound.
anti_patterns: Do not claim optimality from a satisfiable model without complete optimization termination.
Do not accept verification without maximum_makespan or silently turn an objective into a hard bound.
escalate_when: Escalate weighted completion, tardiness, fairness, or multiple objectives to explicit additional objective primitives.

solver_encoding.verification: require maximum_makespan and assert every complete observed job finishes at or before it
solver_encoding.synthesis: assert makespan bounds then emit the typed minimize objective after hard feasibility constraints
formula: makespan >= completion(job) for every subject job

encode_steps: Bind exactly one declared job ID as the subject.
Resolve its eligible machine set, positive per-machine durations, release tick, and deadline tick.
Force every placement outside that declared set or time window to zero.
anti_patterns: Do not infer eligibility from machine names, capacity, or prior schedules.
Do not silently clamp release dates, deadlines, or durations to the horizon.
escalate_when: Escalate sequence-dependent setup, travel time, or calendar exceptions to separate primitives.

solver_encoding.verification: fix the observed assignment and reject any ineligible or out-of-window placement
solver_encoding.synthesis: restrict explicitly declared assignment unknowns to eligible bounded placements
formula: allowed(j,m,t) iff m is eligible(j) and release(j) <= t and t + duration(j,m) <= deadline(j)

rules.summary: Require a predecessor to finish plus its declared nonnegative lag before its successor starts.

authorities.title: Multiproject Scheduling with Limited Resources: A Zero-One Programming Approach

problem_shapes: One finite non-preemptive job must finish before another starts, optionally after a nonnegative lag.
encode_steps: Bind the predecessor first and successor second.
Resolve exactly one matching declared precedence edge and both bounded assignments.
Require predecessor completion plus minimum lag to be at most successor start.
anti_patterns: Do not reverse subject order or infer precedence from input ordering.
Do not claim unbounded temporal correctness from one finite horizon.
escalate_when: Escalate negative lag, start-start, finish-finish, or cyclic temporal semantics to separate primitives.

solver_encoding.verification: assert the finish-to-start inequality over complete observed assignments
solver_encoding.synthesis: enforce the inequality over explicitly declared bounded assignment unknowns

rules.summary: Require one target state to occur within an explicit finite trace bound, supporting bounded witness or unsafe-target counterexample synthesis.

authorities.title: Alloy Language Reference - Commands, Scopes, and Bounded Traces
TLA+ High-Level View - Safety, Liveness, and Fairness

problem_shapes: Find or verify one finite trace that reaches a declared target state no later than an explicit bound.
Treat unsafe states as targets to synthesize a concrete bounded counterexample under separately declared initial and transition rules.
encode_steps: Bind exactly one declared trace ID as the subject.
Resolve target labels and all trace slots against the finite state domain.
Derive the effective bound from parameters.bound when present, otherwise from facts.horizon, and reject bounds outside the declared trace horizon.
Emit a finite disjunction of target membership from index zero through min(bound, trace length).
anti_patterns: Do not interpret satisfiable reachability as inevitability on every execution.
Do not interpret bounded UNSAT as unbounded unreachability.
Do not claim eventual progress, fairness, termination, or absence of infinite cycles from a finite trace.
Do not omit explicit stuttering or termination slots when shorter deadlocked traces must participate in exact-horizon analysis.
escalate_when: Escalate unbounded eventuality, fairness, lasso-cycle detection, or quantified dynamic state creation to a temporal model checker.
Escalate all-executions reachability unless every finite branch and termination encoding is explicitly represented.

solver_encoding.verification: fix a complete observed trace and assert target membership at some index no greater than the effective bound
solver_encoding.synthesis: fill only explicitly unknown bounded slots; SAT is one witness and UNSAT excludes witnesses only for the declared domains and bound
formula: effective_bound = parameters.bound when present, otherwise facts.horizon
exists i in 0..min(effective_bound,L): q_i in G

rules.summary: Require the first state of one finite trace to belong to the caller-declared initial-state set.

authorities.title: State Chart XML (SCXML) - Legal State Configurations and Specifications

problem_shapes: A finite observed or synthesized workflow trace must begin in one explicitly allowed state.
encode_steps: Bind exactly one declared trace ID as the subject.
Resolve the first trace slot and every initial-state label against the finite state domain.
Encode membership as a finite disjunction over the declared initial-state set.
anti_patterns: Do not infer an initial state from naming, list order, or external runtime state.
Do not treat a bounded trace check as an unbounded temporal proof.
escalate_when: Escalate dynamic state creation, quantified process populations, or unbounded initialization semantics outside this finite profile.

solver_encoding.verification: fix the complete observed first state and assert membership in the declared initial-state set
solver_encoding.synthesis: constrain an explicitly unknown first state to one declared initial label within the finite domain
formula: I is a non-empty subset of the caller-declared finite state domain Q

rules.summary: Require every state slot in one finite workflow trace to belong to the caller-declared safe-state set.

problem_shapes: Every state in a finite observed or synthesized workflow trace must satisfy one caller-normalized safety classification.
A symbolic finite trace may be searched for a concrete state that violates the classification.
encode_steps: Bind exactly one declared trace ID as the subject.
Resolve safe-state labels and every trace state against the finite state domain.
Emit one safe-set membership constraint for every state index from zero through the declared trace length.
anti_patterns: Do not infer safety from names or evaluate application predicates that the caller has not normalized into finite states.
Do not report bounded UNSAT as proof for traces longer than the declared horizon.
Do not claim unbounded liveness, fairness, or infinite-cycle safety from finite unrolling.
escalate_when: Escalate arbitrary data predicates that cannot be flattened into a finite safe-state classification.
Escalate universal unbounded invariance to inductive proof or complete model checking.

solver_encoding.verification: fix the complete observed trace and assert safe-set membership at every state index
solver_encoding.synthesis: constrain explicitly unknown state slots to safe labels, or negate this predicate in a separate bounded counterexample query
formula: for every i in 0..L: q_i in S
bounded counterexample condition: exists i in 0..L such that q_i not in S

rules.summary: Require every adjacent state-event-state step in one finite trace to appear in that step's caller-resolved enabled relation.

authorities.title: TLA+ High-Level View - Initial Conditions and Next-State Relations
State Chart XML (SCXML) - Selecting and Executing Transitions

problem_shapes: Every step of a complete finite workflow trace must follow an enabled transition after caller-side guard and priority resolution.
encode_steps: Bind exactly one declared trace ID as the subject and require L events plus L+1 states.
Resolve every trace label and enabled-transition tuple against the finite domains before allocating variables.
For each index i, emit a disjunction matching q_i, a_i, and q_(i+1) against only enabled tuples declared for i.
anti_patterns: Do not evaluate arbitrary guard expressions or SCXML priority inside the solver; callers must normalize them into the per-step relation.
Do not silently allow stuttering, termination, or no-op events unless an explicit tuple represents them.
Do not generalize finite-step validity into unbounded liveness or fairness.
escalate_when: Escalate hierarchical or parallel state machines that have not been flattened into finite configuration IDs.
Escalate quantified, dynamically generated, or infinite transition systems.

solver_encoding.verification: fix every complete observed slot and assert each adjacent triple belongs to its indexed enabled relation
solver_encoding.synthesis: constrain only explicitly unknown state or event slots through the finite per-step transition disjunctions
formula: for every i in 0..L-1: (q_i, a_i, q_(i+1)) in R_i
R_i is supplied after caller-side guard, hierarchy, conflict, and priority resolution

valid.expectation: pass for both observed steps at declared horizon 2
